The test image shows a field-level view of soybean plants. Key observations:
- Whole plant / field view
- Plants show variable height/vigor — some stunted, some normal
- Yellow-green discoloration on some leaves
- Sandy soil visible, patchy plant distribution
- No obvious stem lesions or leaf spots visible from this distance

This pattern of uneven stunting and yellowing in patches is characteristic of soil-borne diseases. Top candidates: **Soybean_Cyst_Nematode** (circular stunted patches, yellowing), **Pythium_damping_off** (patchy poor emergence), or **Sudden_death_syndrome**.

Let me view one reference image — SCN whole plant, as it best matches the field-level patchy stunting pattern.

The SCN reference image closely matches the test image: patchy yellowing, stunted plants interspersed with healthier ones, and variable vigor across the field. The test image shows the same "circular/lens-shaped" pattern of affected plants characteristic of SCN. Sandy soil in the test image also aligns with SCN being worse in sandy soils.
